Direct Harbor recovery trial

Diagnostic only. Production evaluation and Pages remain unchanged.

Download machine-readable results · Frozen input manifests · Workflow evidence excerpts

Decision

One launch integration blocker remains: the stock unprivileged Codex run exits with NonZeroAgentExitCodeError before a recoverable task session. Recover its command-level cause and reconcile unknown usage before another paid attempt. Do not begin the original comparison.

External-boundary and pinned-CLI checks pass. Two credentialed current-arm launch attempts failed; absent was skipped. No completed Codex task or live valid grade was recovered. Existing good (2/2 defects) and weak (0/2) native controls remain valid and unchanged.

Current attempt 1: RuntimeError during installation, no agent-execution timing or effective config. A locally reproduced version-parser defect was corrected once. Attempt 2: pinned version passes; Harbor agent phase lasts 0.614 seconds and raises NonZeroAgentExitCodeError. The offline verifier then reports invalid/artifact, reward 0, Harbor reward_valid=false, measured=false. Harbor returns process zero but the trial wrapper exits nonzero. No rollout, tool call, activation or token observation survives. Whether codex exec itself started is unknown. Absent is staged/preflighted only. No skill revision, effectiveness finding or live comparison is claimed.

Campaign usage

Two credentialed launch attempts consumed 2/4 recovery slots and 2/36 campaign slots; absent was never scheduled. The verified prior record was zero attempts and $0. Attempt 1 failed before agent execution; attempt 2 has no usable usage record or provider invoice. Actual inference request count and cumulative spending therefore remain unknown, not $0. Scheduling stopped. The preflight pair estimate was $2.64 (60k input including cache and 4k output per arm at conservative $20/M input and $30/M output). These rates reserve for cache writes and long-context pricing; they are not observed charges. The operational $20 budget has no verified provider cap. A $4 scheduling threshold reserves $16 for uncertainty/in-flight usage; overshoot remains possible. Runtime and rollout-token limits are not dollar meters.

Sandbox and deployment boundary

Explicit user authorization replaces only the evaluated Codex inner-sandbox requirement with the disposable hosted runner/container boundary. Stock Harbor run/exec methods are inherited without command rewriting. No implementing-agent sandbox or approval mechanism was disabled. Historical Bubblewrap/Landlock failures remain in sandbox.json and are not a current gate.

Actual containers passed UID/GID 1000, CapEff=0, NoNewPrivs=1, Seccomp=2, writable output, fresh-session/auth checks, protected-path absence and deployment hashes. Docker metadata confirms no privilege, no added agent capabilities, cap_drop=ALL, default seccomp (no unconfined override), 2 CPUs, 2 GiB RAM, 256 PIDs, no host PID/network mode and no host mounts. No Docker socket, grader source, reference implementation, mutants or unrelated credential names were available.

Harbor native allowlist restricts the agent to api.openai.com using its separate disposable egress controller; only that controller needs NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW. Credential-free HTTPS requests reached the API root (HTTP 421); GitHub, raw GitHub, Microsoft Learn and the metadata IP failed to connect. This does not prove authenticated Responses API operation or formal network isolation. DNS and the allowed API remain residual channels; web search and remote MCP are disabled.

The inference key must be accessible to Codex and can be read by code in the same environment. Container isolation does not conceal it. No auth file, secret-bearing environment dump, raw agent log or submission is exported. Preflight checks and host metadata are practical evidence, not a formal container-security proof or interactive-workstation equivalence.

The separate offline verifier and protected executable checks are unchanged from the successful controls. Its latest live result is invalid/artifact, not a measured incorrect answer. Host/report metadata validates transport invariants only: integration_valid=true in attempt.json does not assert successful agent execution.

Execution and supporting artifacts

  • Recovery build preflight — Failed before Harbor started: snapshot 503/504 responses and a 600-second image-build timeout. Failure record retained. · Build failure · Image unavailable
  • First native control — Oracle exit 126: script lacked executable permission. Verifier invalid/artifact remains unmeasured. Default sandbox helper was missing; legacy policy rejected. · Native invalid result · Sandbox errors
  • Final native controls and sandbox checks — Good passes and weak fails as expected. Overall workflow failed because both sandbox probes failed. · Known-good pass · Known-weak fail · Sandbox blocker
  • External preflight identity failure — No credentialed task was scheduled. Host inspection selected the network-sharing container by hostname; corrected to the Compose main service and pinned agent image. · Preflight failure
  • First credentialed launch — Both external preflights passed. Current failed installation; absent skipped. Exception RuntimeError, no native agent execution timing. All evidence retained. · Preflight metadata · Current attempt 1 · Absent staging only
  • Focused version-check correction and final launch — Both exact CLI pins pass. Current launch raises NonZeroAgentExitCodeError; invalid artifact grade, unknown usage; absent skipped. No further scheduling. · External boundary checkpoint · Current attempt 2 · Absent staging only

History

Original run 41952213509 explicitly received a runner shutdown signal. Cause remains unknown; exit 143 alone does not identify a Harbor timeout/crash. No original native grade survived. Its prior report is preserved as history below; the prior recommendation is superseded and does not show that the existing stack is better. The prior recovery report at 29f7765 is retained under history, including its zero-spend record and now-superseded native-sandbox requirement. The known-good and weak native observations were not rerun or rescored.

Maintenance and remaining evidence

The prior oracle controls establish a useful narrow grading distinction: both pass the reference; only the good suite detects both defects. The latest invalid artifact remains excluded despite native reward zero and process exit zero. No skill-effectiveness or adoption conclusion follows.

Fourteen focused tests cover native failure/reward validity, unsupported/missing evidence, post-run status/exit, stock launch inheritance, exact-pin version warnings, deployment equality, activation/usage separation and unknown-usage scheduling. No full production suite was run because production code is unchanged.

Custom maintenance: existing staging/projection/report code, a 217-line fixed live runner, 48-line custom-agent class/helper, 14 tests, 29-line snapshot transport helper, branch-only workflow, and historical unused sandbox probe. Two private Harbor overrides (home ownership and effective config upload) remain. No framework patch, but pin compatibility and task checksum deprecation need maintenance. Native egress control requires another pinned sidecar image.

The first host-inspection error and CLI parser correction were integration defects in the trial path. The final native nonzero launch lacks preserved command-level diagnostics because the metadata export was too restrictive. This is an evidence-retention limitation: raw runner-private logs were discarded with the runner, and no new packaging of rejected raw content is attempted.

Existing task prompts, inputs, references, mutants, grader, PowerShell runner and runtime installer are unchanged. Authoring another skill still requires representative tasks, independently executable checks and good/weak controls. Lower maintenance effort has not been demonstrated.

Production components removed: none. If broader adoption becomes justified, overlapping behavioral wrapper/staging/collection might be removable; APM, static checks, protected graders, historical records and publication controls remain.

Smallest next step: a credential-free reproduction of the unprivileged launch setup with allowlisted command-stage/exit diagnostics, followed by reconciliation of any provider usage from attempt 2 before another paid attempt. Do not expand the experiment or retry for a passing answer.
